picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)
picks.rationale: This is the only first-line option in the dossier with a randomised OS result in her histology: mOS 33 vs 24 months, OS HR 0.65 (0.44-0.95), PFS HR 0.41. Both drugs are old enough to have real management playbooks; the profile is myelosuppression, which sarcoma infusion units handle daily with growth-factor support and dose reduction, and the trial's one treatment-related death was in the doxorubicin-alone arm. The hard numbers belong at consent: G3-4 neutropenia 80%, febrile neutropenia 28%, and no published uterine-only effect size. I would not give cycle 1 until someone measures her ECOG, her LVEF, and her pulmonary function against an 8,500 ft baseline; every one of those is currently an assumption or a blank.
primary_concerns: Febrile neutropenia 28% and G3-4 thrombocytopenia 47% on the combination arm; primary G-CSF prophylaxis and an early dose-reduction plan need to be written before cycle 1, not assembled at the first fever
ECOG 1 is an intake assumption and LMS-04 capped entry at 0-1; a measured score could change the whole calculus
Baseline LVEF, hepatic panel, and PFTs with oximetry at her home altitude are all missing, and each one gates this regimen

Six cycles at 60 mg/m2 lands exactly on the 360 mg/m2 anthracycline cap for peposertib (NCT05711615) and approaches the 450 mg exclusion for in vivo lung perfusion (NCT02811523); count the cumulative dose before cycle 6, not after

picks.intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel (first-line fallback if the anthracycline workup fails)
picks.rationale: This is the fallback if the echo or the lung workup rules out full-dose doxorubicin: two generics with over twenty years of sarcoma use and a toxicity profile every infusion nurse knows. GeDDiS settled that it is not better than doxorubicin (46.4% progression-free at 24 weeks, no PFS advantage), so its place here rests on deliverability when an anthracycline is unwise rather than on efficacy. The uterine-specific GOG phase 2 logged one possibly related G4 pulmonary event, which reads differently in a woman with infiltrative bilateral lung disease at 8,500 ft. Do not start it off-protocol without calling MD Anderson first, because prior gemcitabine permanently closes the NCT06498648 phase 2 seat.
primary_concerns: Off-protocol gemcitabine forfeits the abemaciclib trial seat permanently; the Houston call costs nothing and comes first
Pulmonary toxicity signal in the 42-patient GOG study; her lung pattern and altitude thin that margin
No randomised evidence it beats an anthracycline backbone in this disease

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine/docetaxel, randomised phase 2 (NCT06498648, MD Anderson)
picks.rationale: If prefers_trials is going to mean anything in the first-line window, this is the seat I can defend: a standard cytotoxic backbone at a sarcoma center, with abemaciclib carrying a breast-cancer label since 2017 and mature algorithms for its diarrhea and neutropenia. The missing safety datum is specific and worth naming: nobody has published tolerability data for abemaciclib layered on gemcitabine and docetaxel, overlapping myelosuppression is the obvious worry, and this study's phase 1 portion is the first place that combination gets characterized. The randomised phase 2 design means the control arm is the standard backbone, so a seat here cannot leave her worse off than my rank-2 fallback. Contingent on three measurements nobody has made: intact Rb by IHC, a documented ECOG of 2 or better, and confirmation from the site that the treatment-naive stratum is open.
primary_concerns: Rb IHC has not been done; the same stain routes her here if Rb is intact or toward the CDK7 protocol (NCT07633756, after one prior line) if Rb is lost
Combination myelosuppression is uncharacterized outside this study's own phase 1 portion
Single site in Houston, and screening turnaround has to beat the LMS-04 start date

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (planned second line, HRD testing ordered now)
picks.rationale: This is my second-line plan, ranked now so the tissue work that gates it goes out today rather than at progression: overall best ORR 27% (6 of 22; primary-endpoint ORR 23%) and mPFS 6.9 months in exactly her histology, with the randomised confirmation (NCT05432791) fully accrued. Toxicity is heavy on paper, G3/4 neutropenia 75% and thrombocytopenia 32%, but the study managed it with dose modification and reported no treatment-related deaths, and both drugs have long individual prescribing histories. The exploratory RAD51 split (mPFS 11.2 vs 5.4 months) is why her unmeasured HRD and BRCA status matters; the archival-block NGS with an HRD score should ride the same block release as everything else. A 22-patient single-arm study holds a plan, not a promise.
primary_concerns: n=22, single-arm; the phase 2/3 read-out could deflate the signal
HRD and BRCA status unmeasured; without the tissue result the off-label prior-authorization case is weak and the responding-subset question stays open
Both trials of the combination are closed to accrual, so the only live route today is off-label

picks.intervention_label: SBRT to residual lung metastases (consolidation after induction response)
picks.rationale: This is the consolidation card if induction converts her to oligoresidual disease: 7.4% local failure at 24 months with zero G3+ toxicity in the MSK series, and 88% three-year local control in the Cleveland series. That is the gentlest toxicity profile anywhere in this dossier. Both series are retrospective and heavily selected, and her current bilateral infiltrative pattern is not an SBRT target, so this stays sequenced behind a systemic response. Pneumonitis risk gets priced against measured pulmonary reserve at 8,500 ft before any planning CT.
primary_concerns: Retrospective series in selected oligometastatic patients; she is not one today
Contingent entirely on induction response and on the infiltrative pattern proving treatable rather than inflammatory
Pneumonitis layered on an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory lung pattern at altitude is an interaction nobody has data on

notes: What I will not spend the first-line window on: the ivonescimab seat (nct:NCT07516925). Anti-VEGF added to first-line chemotherapy did nothing in this exact disease (GOG-0250, pmid:25713428, HR 1.12), single-agent PD-1 went 0 for 10 in LMS in SARC028 (pmid:28988646) and 0 for 12 in the dedicated uLMS study stopped for futility (pmid:28440953), and HARMONi-2 (pmid:40057343) is an NSCLC result with G3+ treatment-related AEs at 29% vs 16% against pembrolizumab. Trading a phase 3 OS regimen for a 20-patient single-arm study with no sarcoma data is not a trade I can sign. The EZH2 and TCR-T branches stay hypothetical on my board until INI1 and antigen IHC return; a plasma-only SMARCB1 frameshift, read against 170 consecutive INI1-retained uterine smooth-muscle tumours (pmid:34271067), is a stain order, not a treatment rationale. The same goes for ATR: the thesis was tested in ATRX-mutant LMS with biopsy-proven target engagement and patients still progressed within 4 months. The cheap unglamorous moves come before any of my five: block release from the outside institution, one combined IHC requisition (INI1, Rb, MMR, p53, ATRX, PD-L1, B7-H3), tissue NGS with an HRD score, a written ECOG, an echocardiogram, and PFTs read against altitude. Ranks 1 and 2 are alternatives on an organ-function branch, not a sequence; rank 3 competes with rank 1 for the same window, and I would let the measured Rb result and the Houston screening timeline arbitrate that honestly. If LMS-04 proceeds, the team should decide the stopping rule on cumulative doxorubicin before cycle 6, because 360 mg/m2 is both six full cycles and the ceiling on a later trial seat.

picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)
picks.rationale: The only option on the table with phase 3 evidence: PFS HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.29-0.58) by blinded central review, and the 2024 final analysis held up on OS, HR 0.65, median 33 vs 24 months. Open-label design, but central review handles the PFS ascertainment worry and overall survival does not care who was blinded. Two things temper my confidence: uterine LMS was a 45% stratum of a 150-patient trial with no published uterine-only effect size, and the eligibility facts that matter here (ECOG 0-1, LVEF, baseline counts) are all assumed rather than measured in this chart. Even so, nothing else in the dossier comes close on evidence.
primary_concerns: RoB 2 'some concerns': open-label phase 3; BICR covers the PFS read, but post-induction surgery decisions were investigator-driven
No published uterine-only effect size; an LMS-wide HR is standing in for a uterine-specific decision
Single trial, n=150, no independent replication of the combination
Grade 3-4 neutropenia 80%, thrombocytopenia 47%, febrile neutropenia 28%, in a patient with no baseline labs on file and chronic hypoxic adaptation at 8,500 ft
Her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption never scored by a clinician; LMS-04 enrolled ECOG 0-1, so her match to the trial population is unverified

picks.intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel (first-line fallback)
picks.rationale: The fallback with randomised evidence behind it: GeDDiS (n=257) found gem-doc no better than doxorubicin, 24-week PFS 46.4% vs 46.3% with HR 1.28 trending the wrong way, but the regimen is unambiguously active and spares the heart. The 35.8% ORR from the first-line uterine GOG phase 2 is a single-arm number and should not be read as superiority; the randomised comparison is the one that counts. One sequencing fact outweighs the efficacy numbers: her first dose of gemcitabine permanently closes NCT06498648, so if this backbone is ever chosen it should be taken inside that randomised trial rather than off protocol.
primary_concerns: Choosing this over LMS-04 walks away from the only OS benefit ever shown in first-line LMS
GeDDiS PFS HR 1.28 (95% CI 0.99-1.65) trends in doxorubicin's favour
The 35.8% ORR is a 42-patient single-arm phase 2 with open-label response assessment (ROBINS-I moderate)
Off-protocol use forecloses the abemaciclib trial seat; prior gemcitabine is disqualifying there

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (post-induction, NCI 10250)
picks.rationale: The best histology-matched signal in the file, stated precisely: a 22-patient single-arm phase 2 that met its prespecified primary endpoint (5 of 22 responses within 6 months, design 93% power at alpha 0.06), overall ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months. The RAD51-HRD split everyone quotes, 11.2 vs 5.4 months at p=0.05 in 18 assayed patients, is exploratory and carries no weight with me until the randomised phase 2/3 (NCT05432791, accrued, unreported) says otherwise. Entry required a prior line, so this lives after induction, not instead of it. Ordering tissue HRD and BRCA testing now is cheap and makes the later decision an informed one.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I moderate: single-arm, no comparator, open-label response assessment
The RAD51 subgroup is exploratory at p=0.05 in 18 patients and must not be quoted as if prespecified
Grade 3-4 neutropenia 75% and thrombocytopenia 32%, arriving in marrow already hit by LMS-04's 80% and 47%
Her HRD and BRCA2 status is unmeasured; the 4-patient BRCA2 series (pmid:30541756) is tier 4 and cannot carry a selection claim

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine/docetaxel (NCT06498648, first-line trial seat)
picks.rationale: The one first-line trial seat I can defend, and only because of its design: the phase 2 component randomises against gem-doc, so the worst case inside the trial is standard therapy. Abemaciclib itself has essentially no efficacy data in leiomyosarcoma, and the phase 1 endpoint is a blood thymidine kinase time course, so no one should enrol expecting a proven drug. Eligibility currently rests on two unmeasured facts: intact Rb by IHC, a stain she has not had, and an ECOG nobody has scored. Screening costs a stain; enrolling costs the LMS-04 window, and that trade should be named out loud before consent.
primary_concerns: No abemaciclib efficacy data in LMS; CDK4/6 blockade added to chemotherapy is an unvalidated hypothesis in this histology
Rb IHC not performed; eligibility is unknowable today
Randomised phase 2 with a PFS endpoint cannot answer the OS question LMS-04 already answered
Enrolment forfeits first-line LMS-04; that is the real cost of the seat

picks.intervention_label: Pazopanib (later-line anchor, PALETTE)
picks.rationale: For the later-line shelf, the cleanest trial in the whole file: PALETTE was double-blind and placebo-controlled, hit its primary endpoint at PFS HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.24-0.40), and is the one RoB 2 low rating in the dossier. Two deflating facts belong next to that HR: OS did not move (HR 0.86, p=0.25), and the uterine-specific read is a retrospective analysis with ORR 11% and mPFS 3.0 months. Expect disease control, not response. It requires prior chemotherapy, so it anchors the sequence rather than competing for the first-line window.
primary_concerns: No OS benefit in PALETTE (HR 0.86, p=0.25); the 3-month PFS gain is the whole prize
Uterine-specific data are retrospective (ROBINS-I moderate), ORR 11%, mPFS 3.0 months
A 2L+ pick by definition; it says nothing about the first-line decision actually facing this board

notes: What I declined to rank, and why. Ivonescimab first line: HARMONi-2 is a China-only interim PFS result in NSCLC, and the record next to her disease is three misses (SARC028 0/10 in LMS, a dedicated uLMS checkpoint study stopped for futility at 0/12, GOG-0250 showing VEGF blockade added nothing to first-line chemo in this exact disease); trading a phase 3 OS benefit for a single-arm n=20 seat on that record is not a bet I can score as rational. Tazemetostat: the SMARCB1 call is plasma-only at unstated tumour fraction, 170 of 170 uterine smooth-muscle tumours in the one IHC series retained SMARCB1, and even confirmed INI1 loss buys a 9% ORR in the basket's INI1-negative non-epithelioid cohort; the stain is worth ordering, the drug is not worth ranking. The TCR-T axis stops at an unstained antigen, and the one smooth-muscle MAGE-A4 prevalence paper is internally inconsistent and carries an erratum. ATR inhibition already failed as monotherapy in ATRX-mutant LMS despite biopsy-proven target engagement (NCT03718091). Before any ranked option is real, this case needs a scored ECOG, an LVEF, baseline labs, Rb IHC, tissue NGS to settle TP53-vs-CHIP and the SMARCB1 hypothesis, and HRD/BRCA testing.

picks.intervention_label: Documented ECOG score, recorded with resting and exertional oximetry taken at her home altitude
picks.rationale: Every value in her preferences file is an intake assumption, and so is the ECOG 1 that the rest of this dossier screens on. An undocumented score blocks screening at the ECOG 0-1 protocols (IMA203, valemetostat, and the LMS-04 trial population itself was capped at 0-1), and oximetry read against sea-level norms with no altitude on the report is what will fail her at the cell-therapy protocols asking for 90% or better on room air. She lives at roughly 8,500 ft, so a saturation that looks marginal to a screening coordinator may be her baseline, and nobody has written that down anywhere. This is the only item on my list that costs her nothing and closes nothing off.
primary_concerns: If the measured score is 2, a chunk of what this board is arguing over disappears. Better to know that before outreach than halfway through a screening call.
Oximetry without the altitude stated on the result is worse than none, because someone will read it against sea-level references.
A score given verbally does not screen anyone. It has to be in the note.
Preference axes fully satisfied: all of them, trivially, since this forecloses nothing. Preference axes in tension: none. That is exactly why it goes first.

picks.intervention_label: Tissue order B (one block cut: INI1, Rb, MMR, p53, ATRX, PD-L1, B7-H3), sent with orders A and C on a single block-release request
picks.rationale: One Rb stain decides which of the two MD Anderson protocols she can be screened for at all: intact Rb points to the abemaciclib study she is eligible for today, Rb loss points to REC-617 after a first line. INI1 settles whether the SMARCB1 branch exists, and I would rather she learn that from her own tumor than carry a plasma-only call around as a hope. The rate-limiting step is administrative, not clinical: a 2024 block sitting at the hospital that signed it out benign. Orders A and C ride the same release, and ordering them serially is how a first-line window gets spent on paperwork.
primary_concerns: The block release is slow and nobody clinical owns it. Put it in writing this week, name both the 2024 uterine specimen and the 2026 lung core, copy the treating office.

Tissue order A is what makes an off-label olaparib request winnable later. Without a tissue HRD or HRR result the payer file for the best lineage-matched signal she has (27% ORR, mPFS 6.9 months in uLMS) is thin.
Order C (MAGE-A4, PRAME, NY-ESO-1) is not reliably covered outside a trial. Ask self-pay pricing first, and ask the sponsors whether they run their own assay at no cost.
prefers_trials is an assumed value, but this pick survives either answer, since the same results feed standard-of-care decisions.

picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)
picks.rationale: This is the only option in the dossier with an overall-survival number behind it, 33 months against 24, and she can receive it at home rather than in New York or Houston. The assumed efficacy_toxicity_weight of 0.7 would sign off on that trade, but no one has put 28% febrile neutropenia in front of a woman in her thirties who has never had a day of systemic therapy and asked whether she accepts it. That question belongs to her and it has not been asked. If she says yes, do the anthracycline arithmetic before cycle 1: six cycles at 60 mg/m2 lands exactly on the 360 mg/m2 ceiling peposertib enforces, and the Toronto perfusion protocol excludes above 450 mg.
primary_concerns: The empty toxicity_vetoes list is empty because nobody asked, not because she said nothing was off the table. Grade 3-4 neutropenia at 80% and thrombocytopenia at 47% deserve a stated answer from her rather than an inferred one.
Polycythaemia at 8,500 ft will confound anaemia assessment right through induction. Get an altitude-referenced baseline haemoglobin on file first.
LVEF is undocumented and mandatory before an anthracycline, and no laboratory values were supplied at intake at all.
Trabectedin first-line is off-label, since the label wants a prior anthracycline. File the prior authorization as an off-label first-line request up front instead of waiting for the denial.
Uterine LMS was 45% of LMS-04 and a stratification factor, but no uterine-only PFS estimate was published, so her benefit claim rests on the stratified whole-trial analysis.

picks.intervention_label: Ivonescimab (PD-1 x VEGF bispecific), MSK single-arm phase 2
picks.rationale: This is the one protocol in the dossier that writes down what she might actually want: declining standard first-line therapy is an explicit eligibility route, and the ECOG ceiling of 2 tolerates a score nobody has measured. I am not going to move her across the country on it. Anti-VEGF added to first-line chemotherapy bought nothing in her exact disease in GOG-0250, single-agent PD-1 was stopped for futility at 12 uLMS patients, and ivonescimab has no published sarcoma efficacy at all, only a head-to-head PFS win in lung cancer. Worth the phone call this week because the seat closes when LMS-04 starts, and worth taking only if she tells us that repeated flights from 8,500 ft to Manhattan are something she wants.
primary_concerns: All seven sites are MSK New York and New Jersey, and six of the seven carry a Limited Protocol Activities flag. Ask on the first call which visits can happen at her home institution.
Travel is not supplied with the study drug. Ask about MSK patient travel assistance at first contact, not after the first invoice.
prefers_trials true is doing most of the work behind this pick and nobody has confirmed it with her. If she never wanted a trial, this rank is wrong.
Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or VEGF-pathway drugs are exclusionary, so starting pazopanib first would close it permanently.
Preference axis in tension: modality_constraints is empty, which is not the same as her being willing to fly to New York during first-line treatment.

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine and docetaxel (MD Anderson phase 1/2, Rb-intact required)
picks.rationale: The quiet virtue here is that LMS-04 does not close it: the phase 2 admits systemic-treatment-naive patients and the disqualifier is prior gemcitabine, which the planned induction does not contain. So this is the branch she keeps whichever way she answers the first question, which is what earns it a place on a preferences-driven list rather than a pure-efficacy one. Entry needs intact Rb by IHC read on MD Anderson's own antibody, a stain she has not had. Single site in Houston, so the travel question lands here too, just later.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is unconfirmed until the Rb stain reads out. A plasma panel reporting no RB1 alteration settles nothing at an unstated tumor fraction.
Ask MD Anderson whether an outside CLIA Rb result is accepted or the site must run its own G3-245 assay, since that changes the timeline.
If anyone gives gemcitabine and docetaxel off-protocol as her first line, this closes for good.
No efficacy readout exists yet; the phase 1 endpoint is a blood thymidine kinase time course, so she would be trading a published OS benefit for a pharmacodynamic study.

notes: Stating the obvious because it is load-bearing: I have no preferences from this patient. efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7, an empty toxicity_vetoes list, an empty modality_constraints list and prefers_trials true were all defaulted at intake, and the free_text field in preferences.json says so outright. An empty veto list means nobody asked, not that nothing is off the table, and I have tried not to spend it as though it were consent. Goals of care were never discussed either. Five things I would ask her before anything starts. (1) Would you trade 28% febrile neutropenia and 80% grade 3-4 neutropenia for the regimen with the only survival number, or would you rather try something gentler with weaker evidence first? (2) Can you travel to New York or Houston during first-line treatment, and who would go with you? (3) Did anyone tell you that living at 8,500 ft changes how your oxygen readings and your blood counts should be interpreted? (4) Do you want to be on a trial, or was that assumed for you? (5) What would you want us to know about what the last 23 months have been like, given the primary was called benign, in deciding how fast to move now. Ranks 3 and 4 swap if she confirms she wants a trial over standard care and can travel; ranks 1 and 2 hold no matter what she says, which is the only reason I am comfortable ranking a stain and a chart entry above a phase 3 regimen.

picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04), with cumulative-anthracycline bookkeeping
picks.rationale: Nothing else in this file touches a PFS HR of 0.41 and median OS of 33 versus 24 months, and effect size is what I weight. But the real bet is past the median: her disease is lung-only, and a deep response opens locoregional consolidation, the one route that could beat 33 months instead of riding it. So take induction, and count every milligram of doxorubicin, because six cycles at 60 mg/m2 sits exactly on the peposertib cap and creeps toward the perfusion trial's 450 mg exclusion. The uterine-only effect size was never published; I accept the stratified full-trial estimate with eyes open.
primary_concerns: Grade 3-4 neutropenia 80% and febrile neutropenia 28%, in a patient with no baseline labs, no LVEF, and an ECOG that was assumed at intake rather than measured
No published uterine-only effect estimate; the benefit claim rests on the stratified full-trial analysis (uterine LMS was 45% of enrolment)
Anthracycline bookkeeping decides whether the peposertib (<=360 mg/m2) and lung-perfusion (>450 mg exclusion) doors survive induction

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (NCI 10250 regimen), pre-loaded by HRD/RAD51 and BRCA tissue testing ordered now
picks.rationale: The strongest targeted signal anyone has produced in her exact histology: best ORR 27% (6 of 22) and mPFS 6.9 months, with the primary endpoint met and no HRD requirement for entry. The upside case is sharper: RAD51-deficient tumours (9 of 18 assayed) ran mPFS 11.2 months against 5.4 for the HR-proficient, and a genomic series reported 4 of 4 BRCA2-lost uLMS patients with durable benefit on PARP inhibition. Her HRD and BRCA status is the highest-yield unmeasured item in this case; order the tissue testing now so the pivot is loaded before first progression, not after. The subgroup is exploratory at n=18, and I'll take that bet.
primary_concerns: Requires a prior line, so it cannot fill the first-line window; everything hinges on block release from the 2024 outside institution, the stated rate-limiting step
HRD/BRCA status unmeasured; if she lands in the HR-proficient half, expected mPFS is 5.4 months
G3/4 neutropenia 75% on a marrow that will have just absorbed LMS-04

picks.intervention_label: In vivo lung perfusion with doxorubicin plus metastasectomy (NCT02811523), as post-induction consolidation
picks.rationale: This is the swing at long-term survival. Metastasectomy series in sarcoma lung disease report 5-year OS of 36% after complete resection and 55.4% in a uterine subset, and the perfusion protocol was written for her anatomy: bilateral disease, three or more lesions, nothing extrapulmonary, under 65. The clinical base for perfusion itself is a phase 1 built on preclinical work, which I accept because the payoff sits in a category no systemic option in this dossier reaches. Two things can kill it: an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory pattern that a surgeon may call unresectable by wedge, and the cumulative-doxorubicin exclusion above 450 mg that full LMS-04 induction approaches.
primary_concerns: Every lesion in the perfused lung must be resectable by wedge or segment, and the infiltrative radiologic pattern is exactly the finding that defeats that judgement
Cumulative doxorubicin above 450 mg excludes; direct sequencing conflict with full-dose LMS-04 unless cycles are counted from the start
Pulmonary reserve at an 8,500 ft baseline is unmeasured; no PFTs or oximetry on file

picks.intervention_label: IMA203 PRAME-directed TCR-T (NCT03686124), screening started in the first-line window
picks.rationale: Her confirmed HLA-A*02:01 buys entry to the one cellular axis still open, and the phase 1 read is real: confirmed ORR 28.9% in heavily pretreated solid tumours, MTD not reached, severe CRS in 2 of 41. PRAME is the likeliest of the three antigens to come back positive, but nobody has tested it, and the sponsor scores expression on its own IMADetect RT-qPCR assay, so a local stain settles nothing; start that screening conversation now because it takes weeks. No uLMS patient is in the published dataset and median response duration was 4.4 months, and I still want this seat held, because a durable-tail outcome in a woman in her thirties is worth chasing on thin numbers.
primary_concerns: PRAME expression unmeasured; the whole branch can close on one sponsor assay
Protocol requires ECOG 0-1 and exhaustion of (or ineligibility for) standard care; her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption, never measured
mDoR 4.4 months in the interim report, with no uLMS-specific efficacy shown

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine/docetaxel (NCT06498648), held open by an Rb IHC ordered now
picks.rationale: The hedge seat, and the only investigational protocol in this file that stays open on both sides of induction: phase 2 admits treatment-naive patients today, and LMS-04 contains no gemcitabine, so eligibility survives standard induction. The backbone carries real first-line uLMS activity (ORR 35.8% in the GOG phase 2), and abemaciclib on top is the unproven upside. One stain routes everything: entry requires intact Rb by IHC, untested, and the same result decides between this protocol and the Rb-loss CDK7 study. Order the stain now; holding the seat costs nothing.
primary_concerns: Rb status unmeasured; a plasma non-report at unknown tumor fraction is not a negative
No efficacy data for the abemaciclib combination itself; taking this seat first-line would trade an HR 0.41 regimen for an unproven add-on
Overlapping myelosuppression if sequenced straight after LMS-04

notes: The seat I am deliberately not taking is ivonescimab (NCT07516925), even though it is the one protocol that admits her first-line by explicit language. Both of its component axes have already failed in this histology on this file's own record: bevacizumab added nothing first-line (GOG-0250, PFS HR 1.12, pmid:25713428), pembrolizumab went 0 for 10 in LMS (SARC028, pmid:28988646), and a dedicated uLMS checkpoint study stopped at 0 of 12 (pmid:28440953); ivonescimab itself has zero sarcoma data (pmid:40057343). Thin evidence with a live mechanism is a risk I take; a first-line window spent on two mechanisms this disease has already beaten is not. Worth a parallel phone call: whether uLMS is on the CDR404 'selected tumours' list (nct:NCT06402201), since the answer is free and MAGE-A4 IHC rides the same tissue order as PRAME. Every pick above leans on a measurement nobody has made: her real ECOG, baseline LVEF and pulmonary function against an 8,500 ft baseline, HRD/RAD51 for pick 2, PRAME by sponsor assay for pick 4, Rb IHC for pick 5, and a surgeon's resectability read for pick 3. Block release from the 2024 outside institution gates nearly all of it; that request should go out before cycle 1.

picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04 regimen)
picks.rationale: This is the planned regimen, and for once the plan and the evidence line up: LMS-04 gave PFS HR 0.41 and final OS 33 versus 24 months (HR 0.65) in first-line metastatic leiomyosarcoma, most of it uterine. Consensus carriage is real but uneven in age: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS CPG 2021 still reads anthracycline-first because it predates LMS-04, NCCN soft tissue sarcoma carries doxorubicin-based first-line therapy with the trabectedin pairing following LMS-04 (I could not verify the category this run; NCCN blocks automated access), and the KSGO 2025 uterine corpus update makes the combination a strong recommendation in metastatic uLMS. Trabectedin's US label starts after an anthracycline, so first-line use is off-label prescribing carried by the phase 3. I rank it first anyway, because nothing else in this dossier has a randomized OS result in her disease.
primary_concerns: LMS-04 capped performance status at ECOG 0-1, and her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption nobody measured. A documented score has to precede the start decision.
Baseline LVEF and organ-function labs are mandatory before doxorubicin and none exist yet.
Febrile neutropenia hit 28% in LMS-04. Managing that at 8,500 ft, at an unstated distance from the infusion center, needs a plan before cycle 1.
Six cycles at 60 mg/m2 exhausts the peposertib trial's 360 mg/m2 anthracycline ceiling and spends most of the in-vivo lung perfusion program's 450 mg allowance.
Starting it closes the treatment-naive trial window, and the uterine-only effect size was never published (uterine disease was a 45% stratum).

picks.intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel (including the randomized abemaciclib add-on seat, NCT06498648)
picks.rationale: Gemcitabine plus docetaxel is the long-standing NCCN soft tissue sarcoma option in leiomyosarcoma, with a dedicated first-line uterine LMS phase 2 behind it (ORR 35.8%). GeDDiS keeps me honest here: it was not superior to doxorubicin and the PFS hazard ratio ran the wrong way at 1.28, so this sits behind the anthracycline plan as the fallback if the echo or her pulmonary reserve at altitude blocks full-dose doxorubicin. Its real first-line relevance is NCT06498648 at MD Anderson, a randomized study on this exact backbone that admits treatment-naive patients, which honors prefers_trials while keeping the control arm guideline care. That is the trial-seat answer I can endorse from this chair.
primary_concerns: The trial requires intact Rb by IHC and nobody has stained it. The block release from the 2024 outside institution is the rate-limiting step.
Prior gemcitabine disqualifies, so prescribing gem/doc off-trial spends that seat permanently. Completing LMS-04 does not.
ECOG remains undocumented, and the guideline-endorsed population for aggressive doublets assumes ECOG 0-1.

picks.intervention_label: Pulmonary metastasectomy after systemic control (SBRT as the nonsurgical variant)
picks.rationale: NCCN soft tissue sarcoma recognises resection of limited pulmonary metastases in selected patients, and her oncologist already kept local therapy on the table after systemic control. The selection literature is on her side in one specific way: the uterine registry's 5-year OS of 55.4% used a disease-free interval of 12 months or more as its selector, and her interval was about 23 months, while the LMS resection series reached median OS 70 months with repeat operations. SBRT is the guideline-recognised nonsurgical route, with local failure of 7.4% at 24 months in the MSK series. This is a sequenced pick that only becomes real if induction converts an infiltrative bilateral picture into something limited.
primary_concerns: The guideline population is limited, resectable disease. Infiltrative and possibly inflammatory bilateral metastases may never qualify, and that radiologic read also muddies response assessment.
Registry outcomes carry heavy selection bias; there are no randomized data behind metastasectomy in this setting.
The in-vivo lung perfusion variant excludes patients above 450 mg cumulative doxorubicin, which full LMS-04 induction approaches.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (post-induction, NCI 10250 signal)
picks.rationale: The strongest post-induction signal in her exact histology: NCI Protocol 10250 met its prespecified primary endpoint in advanced uterine LMS with median PFS 6.9 months, and entry did not require HRD, so her unmeasured HRD status does not gate it. It is also the pick where I sit furthest ahead of settled carriage, since ESMO 2021 predates the trial and I could not confirm NCCN listing this run, which is why it holds rank 4 rather than 2. Both trials of the combination are closed to accrual, so the live route is off-label prescription of two approved drugs.
primary_concerns: Off-label authorization will go better with tissue HRR/HRD results than with a plasma panel that settles nothing. Tissue NGS on the archival block gates that, and the block release is the delay.
Post-induction positioning only. Nothing on this branch is reachable in the first-line window except the tissue testing.

picks.intervention_label: Pazopanib (later-line, PALETTE)
picks.rationale: Consensus furniture for the later line: NCCN soft tissue sarcoma lists pazopanib after prior chemotherapy, PALETTE showed PFS 4.6 versus 1.6 months against placebo, and the EORTC retrospective in uterine sarcoma saw partial responses only in the LMS subset (11%). Nobody should reach for it now. I include it so the endorsed sequence beyond induction stays visible while the board argues about trial seats.
primary_concerns: No OS benefit in PALETTE.
Positioned after cytotoxic therapy, so it says nothing about the first-line window decision in front of the board.

notes: The window question this board actually faces is one the guidelines do not settle. NCCN's preamble encourages trial participation and ESMO says nothing about sequencing a treatment-naive patient into a phase 2 seat ahead of a regimen with a randomized OS result. My read from the guideline chair: the ivonescimab seat (NCT07516925) asks her to trade LMS-04's OS benefit for a 20-patient single-arm ORR study in a class with a bad uLMS record (SARC028 went 0/10 in LMS and the dedicated uLMS checkpoint study stopped for futility at 0/12), and no guideline in any region carries it in sarcoma. The abemaciclib seat is different. It survives LMS-04 because prior gemcitabine, not prior anthracycline, is the exclusion, so protecting it costs nothing beyond the Rb stain and a documented ECOG. Guideline-carriage audit for this run: the accessibility file's guideline_status fields read accurate as written; the doxorubicin-trabectedin NCCN category stays unverified because NCCN and ESMO web surfaces blocked automated fetches, so I anchored on the primary publications, ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS CPG 2021 (pmid:34303806), and the KSGO 2025 uterine corpus update (pmid:39900346), which makes doxorubicin-trabectedin a strong recommendation in metastatic uLMS. No ESMO-MCBS scorecard for the LMS-04 regimen was verifiable this run, so I cite none. Three measurements keep turning up under every pick above: a documented ECOG, a baseline echo, and the tissue block from the 2024 institution, off which Rb, INI1, and HRD all hang.
